name: LCP61
summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation continued a long-running computational physics project aimed at solving the Löwdin Challenge: deriving the Madelung n+l rule (the empirical observation that atomic orbitals fill in order of increasing n+l, with ties broken by lower n) ab initio from the many-electron Schrödinger equation. The project uses a sealed, parameter-free scalar-relativistic Hartree-Fock field with c = 137.035999 as the only entered constant, running across a chain of sessions with strict protocols for predictions, verification, and provenance tracking.

Session 64 opened by verifying the inherited tree (1091 files, root 9830f18a), then executed M's ruling on fault F63.2: quarantine and rerun of four tie-break control rows at Z=57, 58, 89, 91 using the observed reference configuration rather than the chain's own build. All three predictions (T1/T2/T3) passed, confirming the tie-break departure survives under the physical reference. A resumable per-channel driver (tbstep.py) was built and can-failed when the sealed instrument was killed mid-row by container limits (F64.2). The L2 approximation (point nucleus, infinite nuclear mass) was measured for the first time: the prediction was falsified in that |dD| reached 0.275 mHa at Z=89 and 11.6 mHa at Z=120, far above the 0.05 mHa working floor, though no entrant changed and margin-to-cost ratios remained safe within Z≤108.

The most significant development was a pivot, prompted by M's direct challenge, from ledger-closing work to the core scientific question: why n+l specifically? M proposed treating this as a calibration from hydrogen outward, which led to reparametrizing the ordering rule as n+αl and asking why α≈1. Key findings: α=1 is exactly the critical value of the tie-break clause (100% of α=1 bounds come from equal-n+l pairs); α is set by screening and drifts from 0 at hydrogen toward 1 at neutrality; the periodic table is built entirely at q=1 (neutral atoms), the maximum-screening limit; and α=Δδ (the quantum-defect decrement) is derived, but what sets Δδ≈1 remains open after an orthogonality-counting argument was proposed, tested, and falsified within the session. The 17% of measurements with α<1 are systematic (alkaline earth s→p transitions) and consistent with the tie-break failing specifically at d↔f block pairs. M corrected Claude multiple times for building handoffs prematurely, for drift toward auditable-but-irrelevant work, and for not stating plainly when ongoing computation was not advancing the derivation. M explicitly stated the goal has always been a complete solution to the Löwdin Challenge and that the explanation gap makes the demonstration insufficient on its own.

1	---
     2	name: file-reading
     3	description: "Use this skill when a file has been uploaded but its content is NOT in your context — only its path at /mnt/user-data/uploads/ is listed in an uploaded_files block. This skill is a router: it tells you which tool to use for each file type (pdf, docx, xlsx, csv, json, images, archives, ebooks) so you read the right amount the right way instead of blindly running cat on a binary. Triggers: any mention of /mnt/user-data/uploads/, an uploaded_files section, a file_path tag, or a user asking about an uploaded file you have not yet read. Do NOT use this skill if the file content is already visible in your context inside a documents block — you already have it."
     4	compatibility: "claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cowork — any surface where uploads land at /mnt/user-data/uploads/"
     5	license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
     6	---
     7	
     8	# Reading Uploaded Files
     9	
    10	## Why this skill exists
    11	
    12	When a user uploads a file in claude.ai, Claude Desktop, or Cowork,
    13	the file is written to `/mnt/user-data/uploads/<filename>` and you are told the path
    14	in an `<uploaded_files>` block. **The content is not in your context.**
    15	You must go read it.
    16	
    17	The naive thing — `cat /mnt/user-data/uploads/whatever` — is wrong for
    18	most files:
    19	
    20	- On a PDF it prints binary garbage.
    21	- On a 100MB CSV it floods your context with rows you will never use.
    22	- On a DOCX it prints the raw ZIP bytes.
    23	- On an image it does nothing useful at all.
    24	
    25	This skill tells you the right first move for each type, and when to
    26	hand off to a deeper skill.
    27	
    28	## General protocol
    29	
    30	1. **Look at the extension.** That is your dispatch key.
    31	2. **Stat before you read.** Large files need sampling, not slurping.
    32	   ```bash
    33	   stat -c '%s bytes, %y' /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    34	   file /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    35	   ```
    36	3. **Read just enough to answer the user's question.** If they asked
    37	   "how many rows are in this CSV", don't load the whole thing into
    38	   pandas — `wc -l` gives a fast approximation (it counts newlines,
    39	   not CSV records, so it may over-count if quoted fields contain
    40	   embedded newlines).
    41	4. **If a dedicated skill exists, go read it.** The table below tells
    42	   you when. The dedicated skills cover editing, creating, and advanced
    43	   operations that this skill does not.
    44	
    45	## `extract-text`
    46	
    47	For docx, odt, epub, xlsx, pptx, rtf, and ipynb the first move is
    48	`extract-text <file>`. It emits markdown for docx/odt/epub (headings,
    49	bold, lists, links, tables), tab-separated rows under `## Sheet:`
    50	headers for xlsx, text under `## Slide N` headers for pptx, fenced
    51	code cells for ipynb, and plain text for rtf. Pass `--format <fmt>`
    52	when the extension is wrong or absent (e.g., `--format xlsx` on an
    53	`.xlsm`). If it errors on a file, `pandoc <file> -t plain` is a
    54	fallback; for xlsx/pptx, fall back to the dedicated skill's
    55	Python-based approach (openpyxl / python-pptx).
    56	
    57	## Dispatch table
    58	
    59	Where a dedicated skill is named below, invoke it by name if you have a
    60	Skill tool, or Read its SKILL.md (listed in your available skills, or in
    61	the same skills directory as this file).
    62	
    63	| Extension                         | First move                                           | Dedicated skill |
    64	| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
    65	| `.pdf`                            | Content inventory (see PDF section)                  | `pdf-reading`   |
    66	| `.docx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `docx`          |
    67	| `.doc` (legacy)                   | Convert to `.docx` first                             | `docx`          |
    68	| `.xlsx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `xlsx`          |
    69	| `.xlsm`                           | `extract-text --format xlsx`                         | `xlsx`          |
    70	| `.xls` (legacy)                   | `pd.read_excel(engine="xlrd")` — openpyxl rejects it | `xlsx`          |
    71	| `.ods`                            | `pd.read_excel(engine="odf")` — openpyxl rejects it  | `xlsx`          |
    72	| `.pptx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `pptx`          |
    73	| `.ppt` (legacy)                   | Convert to `.pptx` first                             | `pptx`          |
    74	| `.csv`, `.tsv`                    | `pandas` with `nrows`                                | — (below)       |
    75	| `.json`, `.jsonl`                 | `jq` for structure                                   | — (below)       |
    76	| `.jpg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.webp`   | Already in your context as vision input              | — (below)       |
    77	| `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`         | List contents, do **not** auto-extract               | — (below)       |
    78	| `.gz` (single file)               | `zcat \| head` — no manifest to list                 | — (below)       |
    79	| `.epub`, `.odt`                   | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    80	| `.rtf`                            | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    81	| `.ipynb`                          | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    82	| `.txt`, `.md`, `.log`, code files | `wc -c` then `head` or full `cat`                    | — (below)       |
    83	| Unknown                           | `file` then decide                                   | —               |
    84	
    85	---
    86	
    87	## PDF
    88	
    89	**Never** `cat` a PDF — it prints binary garbage.
    90	
    91	Quick first move — get the page count and determine whether the PDF
    92	has an extractable text layer:
    93	
    94	```bash
    95	pdfinfo /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    96	pdffonts /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    97	```
    98	
    99	`pdffonts` tells you whether text extraction will work before you try it:
   100	
   101	- **No fonts listed** (empty table, just the header) → the PDF is a
   102	  scan or raster export. `pdftotext` and `PdfReader.extract_text()`
   103	  will return nothing useful. Go straight to page rasterization or OCR
   104	  — see the `pdf-reading` skill → "Scanned documents".
   105	- **Fonts listed** → there is a text layer; extract it:
   106	  ```bash
   107	  pdftotext -f 1 -l 1 /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf - | head -20
   108	  ```
   109	
   110	The reason to check `pdffonts` first is user-facing: running
   111	`pdftotext` on a scan produces an empty result, and in a visible
   112	transcript that reads as a failed first attempt before you fall back
   113	to OCR. The two-line diagnostic above costs one tool call and avoids
   114	that — you arrive at the right method on the first try, which is what
   115	a user perceives as "it just read my file."
   116	
   117	That also shapes how to open your reply. The diagnostic commands are
   118	plumbing, not content; lead with what the user asked about. On a
   119	scanned receipt that might be "This is a 3-page scanned invoice; the
   120	amount due on page 2 is $1,845.00," and on a digitally-authored report
   121	it might be "The Q3 report runs 28 pages; revenue on p. 4 is $12.3M,
   122	up 9% YoY." What you're steering away from is the "I'll examine the
   123	PDF" / "Let me check if this is extractable" preamble — the answer to
   124	their question is the first thing they should see.
   125	
   126	For anything beyond a quick peek — figures, tables, attachments,
   127	forms, scanned PDFs, visual inspection, or choosing a reading strategy
   128	— go read the `pdf-reading` skill. It covers content inventory, text
   129	extraction vs. page rasterization, embedded content extraction, and
   130	document-type-aware reading strategies.
   131	
   132	For PDF form filling, creation, merging, splitting, or watermarking,
   133	go read the `pdf` skill.
   134	
   135	---
   136	
   137	## DOCX / DOC
   138	
   139	The `docx` skill covers editing, creating, tracked changes, images.
   140	Read it if you need any of those. For a quick look:
   141	
   142	```bash
   143	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/memo.docx | head -200
   144	```
   145	
   146	Legacy `.doc` (not `.docx`) must be converted first — see the `docx`
   147	skill.
   148	
   149	---
   150	
   151	## XLSX / XLS / spreadsheets
   152	
   153	The `xlsx` skill covers formulas, formatting, charts, creating. Read
   154	it if you need any of those. For a quick look at an `.xlsx`:
   155	
   156	```bash
   157	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.xlsx | head -100
   158	```
   159	
   160	For `.xlsm`, add `--format xlsx` (same zip structure; only the
   161	extension differs). When you need a structured preview in Python:
   162	
   163	```python
   164	from openpyxl import load_workbook
   165	wb = load_workbook("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.xlsx", read_only=True)
   166	print("Sheets:", wb.sheetnames)
   167	ws = wb.active
   168	for row in ws.iter_rows(max_row=5, values_only=True):
   169	    print(row)
   170	```
   171	
   172	`read_only=True` matters — without it, openpyxl loads the entire
   173	workbook into memory, which breaks on large files. Do not trust
   174	`ws.max_row` in read-only mode: many non-Excel writers omit the
   175	dimension record, so it comes back `None` or wrong. If you need a row
   176	count, iterate or use pandas.
   177	
   178	**Legacy `.xls`** — openpyxl raises `InvalidFileException`. Use:
   179	
   180	```python
   181	import pandas as pd
   182	df = pd.read_excel("/mnt/user-data/uploads/old.xls", engine="xlrd", nrows=5)
   183	```
   184	
   185	**`.ods` (OpenDocument)** — openpyxl also rejects this. Use:
   186	
   187	```python
   188	import pandas as pd
   189	df = pd.read_excel("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.ods", engine="odf", nrows=5)
   190	```
   191	
   192	---
   193	
   194	## PPTX
   195	
   196	```bash
   197	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/deck.pptx | head -200
   198	```
   199	
   200	**Legacy `.ppt`** — convert to `.pptx` first via LibreOffice; see the
   201	`pptx` skill for the sandbox-safe `scripts/office/soffice.py` wrapper
   202	(bare `soffice` hangs here because the seccomp filter blocks the
   203	`AF_UNIX` sockets LibreOffice uses for instance management).
   204	
   205	For anything beyond reading, go to the `pptx` skill.
   206	
   207	---
   208	
   209	## CSV / TSV
   210	
   211	**Do not** `cat` or `head` these blindly. A CSV with a 50KB quoted cell
   212	in row 1 will wreck your `head -5`. Use pandas with `nrows`:
   213	
   214	```python
   215	import pandas as pd
   216	df = pd.read_csv("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv", nrows=5)
   217	print(df)
   218	print()
   219	print(df.dtypes)
   220	```
   221	
   222	Approximate row count without loading (over-counts if the file has
   223	RFC-4180 quoted newlines — the same quoted-cell case this section
   224	warned about above):
   225	
   226	```bash
   227	wc -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv
   228	```
   229	
   230	Full analysis only after you know the shape:
   231	
   232	```python
   233	df = pd.read_csv("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv")
   234	print(df.describe())
   235	```
   236	
   237	TSV: same, with `sep="\t"`.
   238	
   239	---
   240	
   241	## JSON / JSONL
   242	
   243	Structure first, content second:
   244	
   245	```bash
   246	jq 'type' /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json
   247	jq 'if type == "array" then length elif type == "object" then keys else . end' /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json
   248	```
   249	
   250	(`keys` errors on scalar JSON roots — a bare `"hello"` or `42` is valid
   251	JSON per RFC 7159 — so guard the branch.)
   252	
   253	Then drill into what the user actually asked about.
   254	
   255	JSONL (one object per line) — do **not** `jq` the whole file; work line
   256	by line:
   257	
   258	```bash
   259	head -3 /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.jsonl | jq .
   260	wc -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.jsonl
   261	```
   262	
   263	---
   264	
   265	## Images (JPG / PNG / GIF / WEBP)
   266	
   267	**You can already see uploaded images.** They are injected into your
   268	context as vision inputs alongside the `<uploaded_files>` pointer. You
   269	do not need to read them from disk to describe them.
   270	
   271	The disk copy is only needed if you are going to **process** the image
   272	programmatically:
   273	
   274	```python
   275	from PIL import Image
   276	img = Image.open("/mnt/user-data/uploads/photo.jpg")
   277	print(img.size, img.mode, img.format)
   278	```
   279	
   280	For OCR on an image (text extraction, not description):
   281	
   282	```python
   283	import pytesseract
   284	print(pytesseract.image_to_string(img))
   285	```
   286	
   287	Note: the client resizes images larger than 2000×2000 down to that
   288	bound and re-encodes as JPEG before upload, so the disk copy may not
   289	be the user's original bytes. For most processing this doesn't matter;
   290	if the user is asking about original-resolution pixel data, flag it.
   291	
   292	---
   293	
   294	## Archives (ZIP / TAR / TAR.GZ)
   295	
   296	**List first. Extract never — unless the user explicitly asks.**
   297	Archives can be huge, contain path traversal, or nest forever.
   298	
   299	```bash
   300	unzip -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/bundle.zip
   301	tar -tf /mnt/user-data/uploads/bundle.tar
   302	```
   303	
   304	GNU tar auto-detects compression — `tar -tf` works on `.tar`,
   305	`.tar.gz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz` alike. Don't hard-code `-z`.
   306	
   307	If the user wants one file from inside, extract just that one:
   308	
   309	```bash
   310	unzip -p /mnt/user-data/uploads/bundle.zip path/inside/file.txt
   311	```
   312	
   313	**Standalone `.gz`** (not a tar) compresses a single file — there is
   314	no manifest to list. Just peek at the decompressed content:
   315	
   316	```bash
   317	zcat /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json.gz | head -50
   318	```
   319	
   320	---
   321	
   322	## EPUB / ODT
   323	
   324	```bash
   325	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/book.epub | head -200
   326	```
   327	
   328	For long ebooks, pipe through `head` — you rarely need the whole thing
   329	to answer a question.
   330	
   331	---
   332	
   333	## RTF / IPYNB
   334	
   335	```bash
   336	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/notes.rtf | head -200
   337	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/notebook.ipynb | head -200
   338	```
   339	
   340	---
   341	
   342	## Plain text / code / logs
   343	
   344	Check the size first:
   345	
   346	```bash
   347	wc -c /mnt/user-data/uploads/app.log
   348	```
   349	
   350	- **Under ~20KB**: `cat` is fine.
   351	- **Over ~20KB**: `head -100` and `tail -100` to orient. If the user
   352	  asked about something specific, `grep` for it. Load the whole thing
   353	  only if you genuinely need all of it.
   354	
   355	For log files, the user almost always cares about the end:
   356	
   357	```bash
   358	tail -200 /mnt/user-data/uploads/app.log
   359	```
   360	
   361	---
   362	
   363	## Unknown extension
   364	
   365	```bash
   366	file /mnt/user-data/uploads/mystery.bin
   367	xxd /mnt/user-data/uploads/mystery.bin | head -5
   368	```
   369	
   370	`file` identifies most things. `xxd` head shows magic bytes. If `file`
   371	says "data" and the hex doesn't match anything you recognize, ask the
   372	user what it is instead of guessing.
   373

# RUNG 0 — THE REVERSE CHAIN
# FROM THE EXACT MANY-ELECTRON SCHRODINGER EQUATION TO `nlchain.step`
# Löwdin Project, Session 63. The deliverable of Challenge criterion 1.
# Every link carries a line-level receipt into the sealed runtime.
# The only number ever entered into this chain is c = 137.035999.

---

## 0 · WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT

The 1969 Löwdin Challenge asks for a derivation of the Madelung n+l rule from the
Schrödinger equation. Sixty-two sessions of this project built and tested a
parameter-free scalar-relativistic Hartree-Fock walk that reproduces the filling
order. **Until this document, the walk existed and the derivation did not.** A
working program is not a derivation; it is an artefact that a derivation must
account for. This is that accounting, written in reverse: from the object that
produces the answer, back to the equation it is supposed to have come from,
naming at every link what was assumed, what was derived, and what it cost.

It is a bridge, not a proof of the rule as a theorem. The distinction is kept
throughout and it is the honest one: **what is derived here is that the ordering
follows from the field, not that the ordering follows from an inequality on n and
l that can be written down without solving anything.**

---

## 1 · THE CHAIN, LINK BY LINK, IN REVERSE

### L12 · `nlchain.main` — THE WALK
    cfg(1) = 1s;  cfg(Z) = cfg(Z-1) + argmin_c D(c)
< truncated lines 138-765 >
not in the list above. A single wrong length falsifies the period-sequence claim
and it must be reported as a failure of the derivation, not smoothed over.

## A2 — THE ORDERING CLAUSE OF MADELUNG
Order the channels by the Z at which each is FIRST entered by the chain. Along that
sequence, **n+l is non-decreasing.**
PREDICTED: zero inversions in n+l over the whole first-entry sequence.
FALSIFIER: any channel first entered after a channel of strictly larger n+l.
This is the primary object of the Challenge and a single inversion is a failure.

## A3 — THE TIE-BREAK CLAUSE OF MADELUNG
Within each block of equal n+l, first entries are ordered by **increasing n**.
PREDICTED: zero violations, over every n+l block the chain reaches.
Prior sessions established this over 26 steps and three distinct pairs (4s/3d,
4p/5s, 4d/5p). PREDICTED HERE over the WHOLE chain, which is the stronger claim
and the one the assembly needs.
FALSIFIER: any equal-(n+l) block whose first entries run high-n before low-n.

## A4 — THE MADELUNG SEQUENCE ITSELF, AS A STRING
The first-entry order predicted, in full, is
    1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p 5s 4d 5p 6s 4f 5d 6p 7s 5f 6d 7p 8s
possibly continuing 5g at or before Z=120 if the field places it there.
FALSIFIER: any departure from this string in the region the chain covers.
**DECLARED IN ADVANCE, BECAUSE IT IS THE HONEST RISK:** the walk is known to
disagree with the OBSERVED configuration at some rows (the `ok=False` rows, the
Cr/Cu-type anomalies). A2/A3/A4 are claims about the CHAIN'S OWN first-entry
order, which is what the derivation produces. They are NOT claims that the chain
reproduces every observed ground state, and must not be read as such. Criterion 7
is answered by A5, separately and on its own terms.

## A5 — THE EXCEPTIONS ARE A FORMAT LIMITATION, AND THE COUNT IS PREDICTED
The `ok` column compares the chain's entrant to the observed differentiating
electron where `ground.py` has a measured configuration.
PREDICTED: the rows scoring `ok=False` are a MINORITY, they cluster in the d and f
blocks, and **every one of them is an element whose observed ground state differs
from the aufbau configuration by the PROMOTION OF AN ALREADY-PLACED ELECTRON**
(s->d or s->f), not by the placement of the differentiating electron in a channel
of different n+l. A one-electron walk cannot express a promotion of an electron it
placed at an earlier Z; the format has no move for it.
PREDICTED count of `ok=False` rows: **fewer than 25 of the scored rows.**
FALSIFIER, and it is the one that would matter: an `ok=False` row where the
observed differentiating electron enters a channel of DIFFERENT n+l from the
chain's entrant AND no promotion of an already-placed electron accounts for the
difference. That would be a genuine counterexample to the rule rather than to the
format, and it must be reported as such, first, before anything else.

## A6 — THE SEED cfg(1) = 1s IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN
`nlchain.py:35` seeds the walk with `d = {(1,0): 1}` and SPEC §3 labels this
CHOSEN. **It is predicted to be DERIVABLE on the walk's own field**, which would
remove the last declared choice from the chain's inputs and is worth the three
solves it costs.
Solving Z=1 with the ruling path (`nlguard.run_guarded`, CORR=False, c=C0) for the
single-electron configurations 1s, 2s and 2p:
    PREDICTED  E(1s) < E(2s) < E(2p),  1s the argmin, by a wide margin
    PREDICTED  E(1s) = -0.5000 Ha to within 1 mHa of exact non-relativistic
               hydrogen, the residual being the scalar-relativistic correction
               (s62 Rung 5 already measured -0.500008079; this must reproduce it)
    PREDICTED  E(2s) and E(2p) near -0.125 Ha, the hydrogenic n=2 value
FALSIFIER: 1s not the argmin at Z=1 -> the seed IS a choice and must stay labelled
CHOSEN in the assembly's ledger. Report it as such; do not quietly keep the label.
FALSIFIER: E(1s) not reproducing s62's -0.500008079 -> a determinism failure, which
outranks this test and is reported first.

## A7 — THE CONSTANT LEDGER IS EMPTY BUT FOR c
Every numerical quantity on the live path from `nlchain.step` down to the C kernel
is DERIVED, PHYSICALLY FIXED, or NUMERICAL (mesh, tolerance, damping). PREDICTED:
the only physical constant is c = 137.035999, and the only quantities that are
neither derived nor physical are the numerical controls whose effect on the answer
has been bounded by Rungs 3, 4 and 7 at <= 0.05 mHa against margins of 32 mHa and up.
FALSIFIER: any coefficient on the live path that is neither derived from the HF
formalism nor a bounded numerical control. That would breach criterion 4 and is the
worst outcome available to this session.

## WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT PREDICT, STATED SO IT CANNOT BE OVERCLAIMED
It does not predict that Rung 2 (the single-configuration bound) will close. Rung 2
is owed and is to be finished inside the assembly; whatever it returns is returned.
It does not predict that the deferred items — the F61.1 55-row re-walk, the Z=59
residue, the coupled 4f2.5d SO check, the s56 2.88 mHa residue, the promotion
operator — will be resolved. They are named as open by M's ruling and stay named.
It does not predict anything about rows above Z=108, which carry PREDICTED labels
and have no measured configuration to score against.

# PREDICTION — RESTART CONTROLS AT THE FOUR TIE-BREAK FIRST-ENTRY ROWS
# FILED SESSION 63, AT CLOSE. Z = 57, 58, 89, 91.
# FILED BLIND. No restart result at these rows has been read by the filing session,
# in this container or reported from any other. `pack64/` is NOT PRESENT in this
# container: tree verified 1089/1089 root=MATCH, nothing written after the s63 seal.
# The existence of a same-shaped result elsewhere is REPORTED BUT UNREAD (F63.2).
# R 1449 / §2.13.

## WHY THIS IS FILED NOW AND NOT BY THE SESSION THAT RUNS IT
s63 §2 restated the project's central claim: the n+l TIE-BREAK clause is false at
n+l = 7 and 8, where the chain enters 5d before 4f (Z=57/58) and 6d before 5f
(Z=89/91), in agreement with measurement at all four rows. That finding rests on
CHAINED-mode rows, whose reference configuration is the walk's own single-
configuration build. The obvious control is restart mode at those four rows, taking
the OBSERVED configuration of Z-1 as reference — the same instrument that closed
Rung 2 (pack53 `ctrl137.jsonl`).

A result of that exact shape has been reported to exist outside this session's
authorship. **Filing this prediction blind is the only action that makes the next
session's run honest whatever that file turns out to contain**, because a
prediction sealed into the s63 root provably predates any reading of any result at
these rows. If the foreign file is later adopted by ruling, it can be scored
against a prediction it cannot have been fitted to. If it is discarded and the
controls re-run, the same prediction serves. Either route is protected.

## WHAT IS PREDICTED
T1 — ENTRANT UNCHANGED AT ALL FOUR ROWS under the observed reference:
        Z=57 -> 5d    Z=58 -> 4f    Z=89 -> 6d    Z=91 -> 5f
     i.e. restart mode reproduces both the chained entrant AND the measured
     differentiating electron, ok=True at 4/4.
T2 — THE TIE-BREAK DEPARTURE SURVIVES: 5d is selected over 4f at Z=57 and 6d over
     5f at Z=89 under a reference configuration the walk did not build itself.
T3 — MARGINS at Z=57 and Z=89 exceed the 0.05 mHa working floor by at least a
     factor of 20, so the departure is physics and not numerics.

## WHAT WOULD FALSIFY, AND IT IS NOT A SMALL RISK
  * Any entrant flipping to the Madelung order (4f at 57, or 5f at 89) under the
    observed reference -> **the s63 tie-break restatement is an artefact of the
    single-configuration reference and MUST BE WITHDRAWN.** Report first, before
    anything else in the session. Rung 2's "ordering is immune" finding would then
    be bounded to n+l <= 6 and could not be extended to blocks 7 and 8.
  * A margin at or below the floor -> the departure is not decidable at these rows
    and the restatement must carry that bound explicitly.
  * Non-convergence -> NO-DATA, not a pass (F59.3 discipline).

## SCOPE
Four rows are four rows. A PASS bounds the single-configuration effect on the
tie-break AT THOSE ROWS and nowhere else. Nothing here licenses a claim about the
other 103 rows, and the s63 assembly's wording may not be strengthened on this
evidence beyond the four elements named.

`nlchain.py:41-49`. The Pauli capacity 2(2l+1) is derived: 2 spin states times
(2l+1) magnetic substates, both of which follow from the angular momentum algebra
of the Schrödinger equation, not from the periodic table.
**CLASSIFICATION: TRUNCATION, defended as a boundary argument (Rung 9, s62).**
The closest excluded channel lies 0.08664 Ha above the winner at Z=19 and 0.15674
Ha at Z=39 — wider at the heavier row — and the excluded region recedes
monotonically in l at fixed n. **COST, STATED: the `order` column is not a complete
ordering of all channels.** At Z=19 the excluded 5s binds at -0.06110, below the
in-space 3d at -0.05807. The entrant is untouched (5s loses by 87 mHa) but this
document may not be read as ranking every conceivable channel. It resolves the
WINNER within a bounded candidate space.

    D(c) = E_HF(cfg(Z-1)+c ; nuclear charge Z) - E_HF(cfg(Z-1) ; nuclear charge Z)

`nlchain.py:65-84`. **Both terms are evaluated at nuclear charge Z** (F40.1): the
reference is the cation of element Z carrying Z-1 electrons, not the neutral atom
of element Z-1. Built the other way, D is a difference between two different atoms
and not a binding energy at all. This is the single most load-bearing convention in
the walk and it was a registered fault before it was a convention.
**CLASSIFICATION: DERIVED.** D is the binding energy of the differentiating
electron; argmin is the variational statement that it occupies the channel in which
it binds most strongly. No rule about n or l enters here.
**THIS LINK ANSWERS CHALLENGE CRITERION 2, THE FILLING AMBIGUITY, EXPLICITLY:**
the walk governs **the differentiating electron**, not the simultaneous ground-state
filling of all electrons. It answers "where does the next electron go", and it
answers it at fixed nuclear charge. Every claim below is a claim about that
quantity and about nothing else.

identically zero and `corr_pot` returns zeros (`hfc2.py:41`).
**CLASSIFICATION: DERIVED (Rung 6 closed s60).** Correlation is OFF, by declaration,
and the solution is claimed at the Hartree-Fock level and not above it.

beta, LADDER = [(0.4,100), (0.2,600), (0.1,1200)], the ruling parameters tried
first so every already-sealed converged number reproduces bit-for-bit.

stored digit**, four orders below the margins the chain decides on.

guard may not return a last iterate; that is the defect it exists to repair.

Take the exact many-electron Schrödinger equation; restrict the wavefunction to a

is not an axiom of the theory and it is not exact. It is what the electron-electron
repulsion does to the hydrogenic degeneracy, and where the two clauses of the rule
disagree with that, the repulsion wins.

# F63.2 — A RESULT ANSWERING THE OPEN QUESTION IS REPORTED TO EXIST AND NO
#         ARTEFACT SHIPS WITH THIS HANDOFF
# Raised SESSION 63, at close, on M's report. Registered before any ruling.
# NOTHING IN THIS FILE ABOUT `pack64/` HAS BEEN VERIFIED BY THE SEALING SESSION.

## THE SPLIT, MADE EXPLICIT, BECAUSE THE WHOLE FAULT TURNS ON IT

**VERIFIED BY THIS SESSION, BY SURVEY (Standing 5):**
    `pack64/` ABSENT from the sealing container      ls -d pack64 -> no such file
    pack sequence present                            5..61, 63   (no 62, no 64)
    tree at seal                                     1089/1089  root=MATCH
    files written after the s63 seal (18:18:53Z)     NONE
    any `ctrl64*` artefact anywhere in the tree      NONE

**TAKEN ON REPORT. SINGLE-SOURCED. NOT CHECKABLE FROM THIS ARCHIVE:**
    that `pack64/` exists at all, in any container
    the filename `ctrl64.jsonl`
    `mode=restart`, `n=4`, `Z=[57, 58, 89, 91]`
    a prediction file stamped 18:46:05Z
    a result at 18:58:06Z, log reading `DONE91 rc=0`
    that the directory is pinned by hash
    that it was not produced by any command the reporting session ran

**NO HASH OF IT IS IN THIS SESSION'S POSSESSION.** It is therefore not pinned from
here, and a future session cannot detect whether it changed between the report and
its own reading. **If M holds that hash it must travel in the next handoff**, or the
"pinned" property is a claim with no artefact behind it — the failure mode this
project has now registered five times.

## THE DEFECT THIS FILE ALSO REPAIRS
`SESSION-63-COMBINED.md` and `PREDICTION-TIEBREAK-CONTROLS.md` both cite "F63.2"
and **no F63.2 document was written.** A referenced fault with no register entry is
R 1670's finding exactly: a practice with no file behind it. This is that file, and
the citations now resolve.

## WHY THIS IS THE WORST MEMBER OF THE F62.1 CLASS
s62 adopted four files of unestablished authorship. That was defensible on a ground
that DOES NOT EXTEND HERE: they were an INSTRUMENT, and every number they produced
was checked against `seedO.jsonl`, already sealed, BEFORE M ruled. There was an
independent thing to check them against.
A RESULT answering the open question has no such check. The only available
comparison is the hypothesis it arrived to confirm, and it is reported to have
appeared AFTER that hypothesis was named, in the directory the next session was
going to create. **That is the shape of a number fitted to a claim.**
Had it been opened and reported as "the four controls hold," the project would have
closed its loudest claim on evidence it cannot attribute.

## WHAT IS AT STAKE, STATED SO THE RULING IS MADE WITH IT IN VIEW
The s63 assembly restates the project's central claim: the n+l TIE-BREAK is false
at n+l = 7 and 8. That rests on CHAINED rows only. The four reported rows are its
control. If they return 4f at Z=57 or 5f at Z=89 under the observed reference, the
restatement is an artefact of the single-configuration reference and must be
WITHDRAWN, and Rung 2's "ordering is immune" collapses to n+l <= 6.

## THE READING DISCIPLINE HELD AND MUST CONTINUE TO
The reported file has NOT been read — not a row, not a clause. Only the row count
and Z set, which were already in the search reduction that raised it. §2.13 is not
recoverable once broken. **No session may read it before M rules.**
`pack63/PREDICTION-TIEBREAK-CONTROLS.md` (sha 0b12ef68…) was filed BLIND and sealed
into the s63 root so the controls can be scored honestly on either route.

## REMEDY — M'S RULING REQUIRED, NOT TAKEN UNILATERALLY
  (a) QUARANTINE AND RE-RUN — **recommended.** Re-derive the four rows under a hand
      that can be named, score against 0b12ef68. Cost: four restart steps at heavy Z,
      minutes each (s61 clocked Z=39 at 79 s; these are heavier), NOT seconds.
  (b) ADOPT BY RULING, as F62.1 — available, but the s62 ground does not extend; see
      above. If ruled, the file must ship WITH ITS HASH and be scored against 0b12ef68.
  (c) DISCARD UNREAD.
Pending M's ruling, nothing is read and nothing is adopted.

## STANDING CONSEQUENCE PROPOSED
Rule 9 gains its converse: **a `packN` must be OWNED by the session that seals as N.**
A missing directory gives a loud false halt (F63.1). An unowned one gives a silent
pass, which is worse. And: **a handoff may not cite an artefact it does not ship or
hash.** This session did, and this file is the repair.

# PREDICTION — RUNG 0 ASSEMBLY: THE CHECKABLE CLAUSES

# SESSION'S TESTS WAS WRITTEN OR RUN. R 1449.
# Scope: the assembly is a WRITING task, but it makes CLAIMS about what the sealed
# chain shows. Those claims are predicted here so they cannot be fitted afterwards.
# Scored only after the sha of this file is verified against the pre-run record.

## WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL FOR A WRITING TASK
Rung 0 is the written reverse chain. A document cannot be falsified by a run. But
the document will assert that the sealed walk EXHIBITS certain structures — the
period lengths, the n+l ordering, the tie-break — and those are readings of data
this session has not yet looked at. **If they are read first and asserted second,
the assembly is a description of what was found, not a derivation that predicted
it.** The Challenge asks for a derivation. So the structures are predicted here,
from the chain's construction alone, and read afterwards.

The chain's construction is fixed and sealed: cfg(Z) = cfg(Z-1) + argmin_c D(c),
D(c) = E_HF(cfg(Z-1)+c ; nuclear charge Z) - E_HF(cfg(Z-1) ; nuclear charge Z),
on the scalar-relativistic average-of-configuration Hartree-Fock field, CORR=False,
c = 137.035999 the only number ever entered. Nothing below is tuned to make it come out.

## A0 — THE CHAIN IS COMPLETE AND CONTIGUOUS
`nlchain.jsonl` carries a row for every Z in 2..120 with no gap and no duplicate:
**119 rows, min Z = 2, max Z = 120, len(set) = 119.**
FALSIFIER: any gap, any duplicate key, or any row whose `ent` is absent.
If this fails, every clause below is void and the assembly cannot be written from
this artefact.

## A1 — THE PERIOD LENGTHS. **THIS IS CHALLENGE CRITERION 2 (period sequence) AND
## IT HAS NOT PREVIOUSLY BEEN EXTRACTED FROM THE WALK.**
Define, using ONLY the chain's own entrant column and nothing from `ground.py`:
a NEW PERIOD begins at each Z whose entrant is an `ns` channel (l=0) with n
strictly greater than every n previously entered as an s channel. Period length is
the difference between consecutive period-start values of Z.

PREDICTED period starts:   Z = 1, 3, 11, 19, 37, 55, 87, 119
PREDICTED period lengths:  **2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32**  and period 8 open at Z=119
                           with 2 rows of it walked (Z=119, 120).

This is the exact sequence the 1969 Challenge names. It is predicted to fall out of
the entrant column with no shell-capacity rule imposed and no period boundary
defined in the code — `nlchain.py` contains no notion of a period anywhere.
FALSIFIER: any length differing from 2,8,8,18,18,32,32, or a period start at a Z

#!/bin/bash
# open58.sh -- THE OPEN, CONDENSED.  s58, on M's ruling.
#
# THE RULE THIS ENCODES:
#   ACCEPT THE HANDOFF AS SEALED.  PICK UP WHERE THE LAST SESSION ENDED.
#   DO NOT RE-PROVE THE CHAIN AT EVERY OPEN.
#
# What s57's open did, and what it cost, every session:
#     manifest verify        1140 files, both halves
#     smoke gates            13 serial, incl. nlguard 94s + gate7980 23s
#     full replay 1..71      ~3 min detached + poll cycles
#   The replay and the manifest are REDUNDANT WITH EACH OTHER.  Identical bytes
#   plus deterministic code give identical output; the hash already proved the
#   bytes.  The replay's only unique job -- catching compiler/interpreter drift --
#   is done by ONE canary in ~1 s.
#
# What this does instead:
#     STEP 1  seal      current manifest only.  History lives in LINEAGE.txt.
#     STEP 2  runtime   rebuild rt/ from sealed packs.
#     STEP 3  canary    environment drift, ~1 s.
#   Total: seconds, not minutes.  The full replay runs ONCE, at SEAL time
#   (pack58/seal58.sh), where it belongs -- proving what is being handed over,
#   not re-proving what was already handed over.
#
# ESCALATION: if the canary reports DRIFT, and only then, run the full replay.
set -u
FAIL(){ echo; echo "!!! OPEN HALTED: $1"; echo "Fix before any work."; exit 1; }
N=$(ls -d pack* 2>/dev/null | sed 's/pack//' | sort -n | tail -1)

echo "=== STEP 1 · SEAL (current only) ================================="
python3 pack58/condense.py ${N} --check || FAIL "seal check failed"

echo "=== STEP 2 · RUNTIME ============================================="
if [ ! -f rt/nlchain.jsonl ]; then
  mkdir -p rt && cp -r pack5/. rt/ && cp pack7/pack5/*.py rt/ && cp -r pack8/pack5fix/. rt/
  cp pack9/*.py pack9/*.jsonl rt/ && cp pack10/* rt/ && cp pack12/*.py pack13/*.py rt/
  cp pack16/*.py pack16/*.jsonl rt/ && cp pack17/*.py pack17/*.jsonl pack17/*.c rt/
  cp pack18/*.py pack18/*.jsonl pack18/*.c rt/
  for n in $(seq 19 $N); do for e in py jsonl c json sh; do ls pack$n/*.$e >/dev/null 2>&1 && cp pack$n/*.$e rt/; done; done
  ( cd rt && for k in shoot shoot_sr shoot_x; do gcc -O2 -shared -fPIC -o lib$k.so $k.c || exit 1; done ) \
    || FAIL "kernel compile failed"
fi
[ -f rt/prime.py ] && [ -f rt/run.sh ] || FAIL "prime.py / run.sh missing"
( cd rt && python3 prime.py 2>&1 | tail -3 )

echo "=== STEP 3 · CANARY (environment drift) =========================="
python3 pack58/canary.py || FAIL "environment drift -- NOW run pack55/gates_run55.sh 1 71"

echo
echo "=== OPEN COMPLETE ================================================"
echo "  The chain is sealed and the environment reproduces it."
echo "  Do NOT re-verify history. Work list is §6 of the s58 bridge."
echo
echo "  STANDING (s58):"
echo "    * Seal:     python3 pack58/condense.py N --seal   (never sed a verify script)"
echo "    * Retire:   undeclared removals HALT the seal. Declare in pack<N>/RETIRE.txt."
echo "    * Surveys:  counts, sets, diffs -- pack57/rd.py. Never a row dump."
echo "    * Replay:   at SEAL time only, or when the canary reports DRIFT."

**All four control rows are in. T1, T2 and T3 all hold. The s63 restatement survives.**

```
Z=57  ent 5d   rec 5d   ok=True   D=-0.20585   margin 67.56 mHa   4f at -0.10556
Z=58  ent 4f   rec 4f   ok=True
Z=89  ent 6d   rec 6d   ok=True   D=-0.15762   margin 32.33 mHa   5f at -0.03146
Z=91  ent 5f   rec 5f   ok=True   D=-0.30535   margin 81.95 mHa
```

Scored against `0b12ef68…` (sha verified at the open, before any row was read):

- **T1 — PASS.** Entrant unchanged at all four rows under the observed reference, ok=True at 4/4.
- **T2 — PASS.** 5d over 4f at Z=57 by **100.29 mHa**; 6d over 5f at Z=89 by **126.16 mHa**. The tie-break departure survives a reference configuration the walk did not build itself.
- **T3 — PASS, with room.** Predicted ≥20× the 0.05 mHa floor. Actual: 1351× at Z=57 and 647× at Z=89 on the entrant margin; 2005× and 2523× on the 5d/4f and 6d/5f gaps themselves. Physics, not numerics.

No row falsified. The departure is not an artefact of the single-configuration reference, so Rung 2's immunity finding stands at n+l = 7 and 8 rather than collapsing to ≤ 6.

**Two things happened in the running that need registering, not smoothing over.**

**F64.2 — the detached run was killed mid-row.** `nlchain.py restart Z` is one indivisible process per row, and at Z=89 it exceeds what a single call gets here; it died after ten converged channels with all of them thrown away. Repair: `pack64/tbstep.py`, which divides the row into its channels and writes each before the next begins — §2.20 one level down. It calls the sealed functions unmodified; `nlchain.py` was not edited. **Can-failed before use: it reproduces `nlchain.py restart` bit-for-bit at Z=57 and Z=58, every field but `sec` and the added `driver` provenance field.** Z=89 and Z=91 were run on it; Z=57 and Z=58 in `tbctrl64.jsonl` are the sealed instrument's own output.

Also worth having in view: a killed process left a complete Z=57 row on disk. I did not use it. Z=57 was re-run, and the re-run is **identical to the orphan in every field including `sec`** — a determinism receipt I did not go looking for, kept as `.row57.orphan`.

**Output is `pack64/tbctrl64.jsonl`, deliberately not the reported `ctrl64.jsonl`.** Nothing of the quarantined artefact was read. I'd propose `ctrl64.jsonl` becomes a reserved name no session may write, so a future session finding both can tell them apart without opening either.

Ruling 2 is yours when you want it. Also still open from the survey: **F64.1** — the s63 handoff quotes its own tree as 1089 where LINEAGE and the open both give 1091. Third instance of that shape.

usage: python3 nlchain.py Zstart Zstop      appends nlchain.jsonl (key Z). No constant.
       python3 nlchain.py restart Z         one step from OBSERVED config(Z-1) (per-element test, not chained)

import sys, os, json, time

    d[c] = d.get(c, 0) + 1

    cands = candidates(cfg_prev)
    t0 = time.time()
    # F40.1: the reference is the CATION of element Z carrying config(Z-1) -- nuclear charge Z, Z-1 electrons.
    # Building it at nuclear charge Z-1 makes D a difference between two different atoms, not a binding energy.
    # s48: EVERY solve goes through the guard (F47.2). Rung 0 IS the ruling field and is
    # tried first, so a converging channel returns exactly the unguarded number. A channel
    # converging at NO rung returns no number and joins `fail`, beside the node-count ones.
    gr = NG.run_guarded(Z, cfg_prev, 'ref')

#!/bin/bash
# tb64.sh -- SESSION 64, F63.2 remedy (a): the four tie-break control rows, RE-RUN.
# Sealed instrument, unmodified: rt/nlchain.py restart Z (observed cfg(Z-1) reference).
# Scored later against pack63/PREDICTION-TIEBREAK-CONTROLS.md sha 0b12ef68...
# §2.20: one row at a time, each written before the next begins, resumable, bounded.
# NOTE: output is tbctrl64.jsonl. ctrl64.jsonl is a QUARANTINED name -- never write it.
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
OUT="$HERE/tbctrl64.jsonl"
LOG="$HERE/tb64.log"
BUDGET=1800
touch "$OUT"
cd "$HERE/../rt"
for Z in 57 58 89 91; do
  if grep -q "\"Z\": $Z," "$OUT" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "SKIP Z=$Z (already written)" | tee -a "$LOG"; continue
  fi
  echo "START Z=$Z $(date -u +%FT%TZ) budget=${BUDGET}s" | tee -a "$LOG"
  t0=$(date +%s)
  timeout $BUDGET python3 nlchain.py restart $Z > "$HERE/.row$Z.tmp" 2>>"$LOG"
  rc=$?
  t1=$(date +%s)
  if [ $rc -eq 124 ]; then
    echo "OVERRUN Z=$Z rc=124 after $((t1-t0))s -- NO-DATA, not a fail" | tee -a "$LOG"
    rm -f "$HERE/.row$Z.tmp"; continue
  fi
  if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR Z=$Z rc=$rc after $((t1-t0))s -- NO-DATA" | tee -a "$LOG"
    rm -f "$HERE/.row$Z.tmp"; continue
  fi
  tail -1 "$HERE/.row$Z.tmp" >> "$OUT"
  rm -f "$HERE/.row$Z.tmp"
  echo "DONE$Z rc=0 $((t1-t0))s $(date -u +%FT%TZ)" | tee -a "$LOG"
done
echo "TB64 COMPLETE $(date -u +%FT%TZ) rows=$(wc -l < "$OUT")" | tee -a "$LOG"

input.description: Resumable per-channel driver so heavy rows can survive call boundaries
input.file_text:
"""tbstep.py -- SESSION 64. A RESUMABLE restart-mode step. §2.20 at channel granularity.

WHY THIS EXISTS. `nlchain.py restart Z` is one indivisible process per row. At Z=89 and
Z=91 it exceeds the wall-clock a single call in this container gets, and is killed
part-way with every converged channel thrown away (F64.2). This driver divides the row
into its channels, writes each channel's result before the next begins, and on a rerun
costs only what has not succeeded. That is the prime directive applied one level down.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. It does not touch the instrument. It calls the SAME sealed
functions -- nlchain.candidates, nlchain.add, nlchain.tagof, nlguard.run_guarded,
ground.expand -- with the same arguments in the same order, and assembles the record
with the same expressions as nlchain.step. `nlchain.py` is not edited or sed-ed (rule 4).

CAN-FAIL / CONTROL. It is not used on a row until it has REPRODUCED `nlchain.py restart`
bit-for-bit on a row that instrument already returned (Z=57, Z=58), every field but the
two named below. If it cannot reproduce those, it is not an instrument and is discarded.

TWO FIELDS DIFFER BY CONSTRUCTION AND ARE EXCLUDED FROM THAT COMPARISON:
  sec     -- in nlchain.step this is the wall time of one process. Here it is the SUM of
             compute seconds over the channels, which may be spread across several calls.
  driver  -- present here, absent there. Provenance (§2.11); a resumed row must say so.

usage: python3 tbstep.py Z [--budget SECONDS]
       Runs missing channels until the budget is spent, writing the cache as it goes.
       Prints the assembled row to stdout ONLY when every channel is resolved.
       Otherwise prints PARTIAL and the count remaining, and exits 3.
"""
import sys, os, json, time

os.environ.setdefault("SIC_NOCLAMP", "1"); os.environ.setdefault("SUBCELL", "1")
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..', 'rt'))
import hfc2 as H
import ground as G
import nlguard as NG
import nlchain as C
H.CORR = False

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def cache_path(Z):
    return os.path.join(HERE, f".cache_Z{Z}.json")


def load_cache(Z):
    p = cache_path(Z)
    return json.load(open(p)) if os.path.exists(p) else {}


def save_cache(Z, c):
    p = cache_path(Z)
    json.dump(c, open(p + '.tmp', 'w'))
    os.replace(p + '.tmp', p)          # atomic: a killed write cannot corrupt the cache


def main():
    Z = int(sys.argv[1])
    budget = 1800
    if '--budget' in sys.argv:
        budget = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--budget') + 1])
    t_start = time.time()

    cfg_prev = G.expand(Z - 1)                       # restart mode: OBSERVED cfg(Z-1)
    cands = C.candidates(cfg_prev)
    cache = load_cache(Z)

    # --- the reference: cation of element Z carrying Z-1 electrons (F40.1) ---
    if 'ref' not in cache:
        t1 = time.time()
        gr = NG.run_guarded(Z, cfg_prev, 'ref')
        if not gr['conv']:
            print(f"NO-DATA Z={Z}: reference did not converge -- {gr['err']}")
            sys.exit(4)
        cache['ref'] = dict(E=gr['E'], it=gr['it'], rung=gr['rung'], sec=int(time.time() - t1))
        save_cache(Z, cache)
        print(f"    {Z} ref E={gr['E']} it={gr['it']} rung={gr['rung']}", flush=True)
    Eref = cache['ref']['E']

    # --- the channels, one at a time, written before the next begins ---
    for c in cands:
        tag = C.tagof(c)
        if tag in cache:
            continue
        if time.time() - t_start > budget:
            break
        t1 = time.time()
        g = NG.run_guarded(Z, C.add(cfg_prev, c), tag)
        if g['conv']:
            cache[tag] = dict(nl=list(c), D=round(g['E'] - Eref, 5), it=g['it'],
                              rung=g['rung'], sec=int(time.time() - t1))
        else:
            cache[tag] = dict(nl=list(c), D=None, err=g['err'], rung=g['rung'],
                              sec=int(time.time() - t1))
        save_cache(Z, cache)
        print(f"    {Z} {tag:>3} {cache[tag].get('D')} rung {cache[tag].get('rung')}", flush=True)

    missing = [C.tagof(c) for c in cands if C.tagof(c) not in cache]
    if missing:
        print(f"PARTIAL Z={Z} remaining={len(missing)} {missing}")
        sys.exit(3)

    # --- assembly, expression for expression as nlchain.step ---
    D = {C.tagof(c): cache[C.tagof(c)] for c in cands}
    ok = {k: v for k, v in D.items() if v.get('D') is not None}
    if not ok:
        print(f"NO-DATA Z={Z}: no channel converged")
        sys.exit(4)
    win = min(ok, key=lambda k: ok[k]['D'])
    srt = sorted(ok, key=lambda k: ok[k]['D'])
    marg = round(ok[srt[1]]['D'] - ok[srt[0]]['D'], 5) if len(srt) > 1 else None
    try:
        rec = ''.join(f"{n}{'spdfg'[l]}{k}" for n, l, k in G.expand(Z))
        cz = {(n, l): k for n, l, k in G.expand(Z)}
        cz1 = {(n, l): k for n, l, k in G.expand(Z - 1)}
        recent = [nl for nl in cz if cz[nl] > cz1.get(nl, 0) + 1e-9] if Z > 1 else []
        rectag = C.tagof(recent[0]) if len(recent) == 1 else None
        prov = 'OBSERVED'
    except (KeyError, IndexError):
        rec, rectag, prov = None, None, ('SYNTHESISED-UNMEASURED' if Z <= 118 else 'PREDICTED-UNSYNTHESISED')
    total_sec = cache['ref']['sec'] + sum(v['sec'] for v in D.values())
    o = dict(Z=Z, mode='restart', ent=win, ent_nl=ok[win]['nl'], D_ent=ok[win]['D'], margin=marg,
             order=[[k, ok[k]['D']] for k in srt], nfail=len(D) - len(ok),
             fail={k: v['err'] for k, v in D.items() if v.get('D') is None},
             ref_cfg=''.join(f"{n}{'spdfg'[l]}{k}" for n, l, k in cfg_prev),
             rec_ent=rectag, rec_cfg=rec, prov=prov,
             label=('PREDICTED-BY-FIELD' if prov != 'OBSERVED' else 'CHAIN'),
             ok=(rectag == win) if rectag else None, it_ref=cache['ref']['it'], sec=total_sec,
             rung_ref=cache['ref']['rung'],
             chan={k: dict(it=v.get('it'), rung=v.get('rung')) for k, v in D.items()},
             rungs=sorted({v.get('rung') for v in D.values()} | {cache['ref']['rung']}),
             guard='nlguard LADDER=' + repr(NG.LADDER),
             driver='pack64/tbstep.py resumable per-channel; sec is summed compute time')
    print(json.dumps(o))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import nlguard as NG
import nlchain as C
H.CORR = False

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def cache_path(Z):
    return os.path.join(HERE, f".cache_Z{Z}.json")


def load_cache(Z):
    p = cache_path(Z)
    return json.load(open(p)) if os.path.exists(p) else {}


def save_cache(Z, c):
    p = cache_path(Z)
    json.dump(c, open(p + '.tmp', 'w'))
    os.replace(p + '.tmp', p)          # atomic: a killed write cannot corrupt the cache


def main():
    Z = int(sys.argv[1])
    budget = 1800
    if '--budget' in sys.argv:
        budget = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--budget') + 1])
    t_start = time.time()

    cfg_prev = G.expand(Z - 1)                       # restart mode: OBSERVED cfg(Z-1)
    cands = C.candidates(cfg_prev)
    cache = load_cache(Z)

    # --- the reference: cation of element Z carrying Z-1 electrons (F40.1) ---
    if 'ref' not in cache:
        t1 = time.time()
        gr = NG.run_guarded(Z, cfg_prev, 'ref')
        if not gr['conv']:
            print(f"NO-DATA Z={Z}: reference did not converge -- {gr['err']}")
            sys.exit(4)
        cache['ref'] = dict(E=gr['E'], it=gr['it'], rung=gr['rung'], sec=int(time.time() - t1))
        save_cache(Z, cache)
        print(f"    {Z} ref E={gr['E']} it={gr['it']} rung={gr['rung']}", flush=True)
    Eref = cache['ref']['E']

    # --- the channels, one at a time, written before the next begins ---
    for c in cands:
        tag = C.tagof(c)
        if tag in cache:
            continue
        if time.time() - t_start > budget:
            break
        t1 = time.time()
        g = NG.run_guarded(Z, C.add(cfg_prev, c), tag)
        if g['conv']:
            cache[tag] = dict(nl=list(c), D=round(g['E'] - Eref, 5), it=g['it'],
                              rung=g['rung'], sec=int(time.time() - t1))
        else:
            cache[tag] = dict(nl=list(c), D=None, err=g['err'], rung=g['rung'],
                              sec=int(time.time() - t1))
        save_cache(Z, cache)
        print(f"    {Z} {tag:>3} {cache[tag].get('D')} rung {cache[tag].get('rung')}", flush=True)

    missing = [C.tagof(c) for c in cands if C.tagof(c) not in cache]
    if missing:
        print(f"PARTIAL Z={Z} remaining={len(missing)} {missing}")
        sys.exit(3)

    # --- assembly, expression for expression as nlchain.step ---
    D = {C.tagof(c): cache[C.tagof(c)] for c in cands}
    ok = {k: v for k, v in D.items() if v.get('D') is not None}
    if not ok:
        print(f"NO-DATA Z={Z}: no channel converged")
        sys.exit(4)
    win = min(ok, key=lambda k: ok[k]['D'])
    srt = sorted(ok, key=lambda k: ok[k]['D'])
    marg = round(ok[srt[1]]['D'] - ok[srt[0]]['D'], 5) if len(srt) > 1 else None
    try:
        rec = ''.join(f"{n}{'spdfg'[l]}{k}" for n, l, k in G.expand(Z))
        cz = {(n, l): k for n, l, k in G.expand(Z)}
        cz1 = {(n, l): k for n, l, k in G.expand(Z - 1)}
        recent = [nl for nl in cz if cz[nl] > cz1.get(nl, 0) + 1e-9] if Z > 1 else []
        rectag = C.tagof(recent[0]) if len(recent) == 1 else None
        prov = 'OBSERVED'
    except (KeyError, IndexError):
        rec, rectag, prov = None, None, ('SYNTHESISED-UNMEASURED' if Z <= 118 else 'PREDICTED-UNSYNTHESISED')
    total_sec = cache['ref']['sec'] + sum(v['sec'] for v in D.values())
    o = dict(Z=Z, mode='restart', ent=win, ent_nl=ok[win]['nl'], D_ent=ok[win]['D'], margin=marg,
             order=[[k, ok[k]['D']] for k in srt], nfail=len(D) - len(ok),
             fail={k: v['err'] for k, v in D.items() if v.get('D') is None},
             ref_cfg=''.join(f"{n}{'spdfg'[l]}{k}" for n, l, k in cfg_prev),
             rec_ent=rectag, rec_cfg=rec, prov=prov,
             label=('PREDICTED-BY-FIELD' if prov != 'OBSERVED' else 'CHAIN'),
             ok=(rectag == win) if rectag else None, it_ref=cache['ref']['it'], sec=total_sec,
             rung_ref=cache['ref']['rung'],
             chan={k: dict(it=v.get('it'), rung=v.get('rung')) for k, v in D.items()},
             rungs=sorted({v.get('rung') for v in D.values()} | {cache['ref']['rung']}),
             guard='nlguard LADDER=' + repr(NG.LADDER),
             driver='pack64/tbstep.py resumable per-channel; sec is summed compute time')
    print(json.dumps(o))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""tbscore.py -- SESSION 64. Scores pack64/tbctrl64.jsonl against
pack63/PREDICTION-TIEBREAK-CONTROLS.md, sha 0b12ef684c1e39b3b26fc9d0ebf988cda1929e2e658047f8ee2e3b88f0b61c20.

The prediction's three clauses, transcribed and not paraphrased:
  T1  entrant unchanged at all four rows under the OBSERVED reference:
      Z=57 -> 5d, Z=58 -> 4f, Z=89 -> 6d, Z=91 -> 5f, and ok=True at 4/4.
  T2  the tie-break departure survives: 5d selected over 4f at Z=57, 6d over 5f at Z=89.
  T3  margins at Z=57 and Z=89 exceed the 0.05 mHa working floor by at least 20x.

FALSIFIERS, also from the prediction, checked explicitly rather than left implicit:
  * any entrant flipping to the Madelung order (4f at 57, 5f at 89)  -> WITHDRAW s63
  * a margin at or below the floor                                   -> NOT DECIDABLE
  * non-convergence of a row                                         -> NO-DATA, not a pass

usage: python3 tbscore.py                 score the sealed rows
       python3 tbscore.py --canfail       run the injected-failure controls and exit
A scorer that cannot go red is not a scorer (s63, SCORE-RUNG-0-ASSEMBLY §CONTROLS).
"""
import sys, os, json, hashlib

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
PRED = os.path.join(HERE, '..', 'pack63', 'PREDICTION-TIEBREAK-CONTROLS.md')
PRED_SHA = '0b12ef684c1e39b3b26fc9d0ebf988cda1929e2e658047f8ee2e3b88f0b61c20'
ROWS = os.path.join(HERE, 'tbctrl64.jsonl')
FLOOR = 0.00005          # 0.05 mHa, in Ha. Rung 7 grid floor / s61 seed-memory floor.

T1 = {57: '5d', 58: '4f', 89: '6d', 91: '5f'}
MADELUNG = {57: '4f', 89: '5f'}      # what the tie-break clause would have required
T2_PAIRS = {57: ('5d', '4f'), 89: ('6d', '5f')}


def verify_prediction():
    h = hashlib.sha256(open(PRED, 'rb').read()).hexdigest()
    if h != PRED_SHA:
        print(f"HALT: prediction sha {h[:12]}... != filed {PRED_SHA[:12]}...")
        sys.exit(1)
    return h


def score(rows):
    """rows: {Z: record}. Returns (verdict, lines). Verdict PASS / WITHDRAW / NOT-DECIDABLE / NO-DATA."""
    out, verdict = [], 'PASS'
    Dof = lambda r: dict(r['order'])

    # --- falsifier 1, checked FIRST because the prediction says report it first ---
    flipped = [Z for Z, tag in MADELUNG.items()
               if Z in rows and rows[Z]['ent'] == tag]
    if flipped:
        out.append(f"  FALSIFIED  entrant flipped to Madelung order at Z={flipped}")
        out.append("  ** THE s63 TIE-BREAK RESTATEMENT MUST BE WITHDRAWN. **")
        return 'WITHDRAW', out

    missing = [Z for Z in T1 if Z not in rows]
    if missing:
        out.append(f"  NO-DATA    rows absent: {missing}")
        return 'NO-DATA', out

    # --- T1 ---
    bad = [(Z, rows[Z]['ent'], t) for Z, t in T1.items() if rows[Z]['ent'] != t]
    nok = sum(1 for Z in T1 if rows[Z]['ok'] is True)
    if bad:
        out.append(f"  T1  FAIL   entrant differs: {bad}")
        verdict = 'FAIL'
    else:
        out.append(f"  T1  PASS   entrant unchanged 4/4; ok=True {nok}/4")
        if nok != 4:
            out.append(f"  T1  FAIL   ok=True only {nok}/4")
            verdict = 'FAIL'

    # --- T2 ---
    for Z, (w, l) in T2_PAIRS.items():
        D = Dof(rows[Z])
        if w not in D or l not in D:
            out.append(f"  T2  NO-DATA Z={Z}: {w} or {l} did not converge")
            verdict = 'NO-DATA' if verdict == 'PASS' else verdict
            continue
        gap = D[l] - D[w]
        ok = gap > 0
        out.append(f"  T2  {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}   Z={Z}: {w} over {l} by "
                   f"{gap*1000:.2f} mHa  ({gap/FLOOR:.0f}x floor)")
        if not ok:
            verdict = 'FAIL'

    # --- T3 ---
    for Z in (57, 89):
        m = rows[Z]['margin']
        if m is None:
            out.append(f"  T3  NO-DATA Z={Z}: no runner-up")
            continue

# F64.1 — THE s63 HANDOFF QUOTES A TREE COUNT ITS OWN TREE NO LONGER HAD
# Raised 2026-08-20, SESSION 64, at the open, by survey, before any work.
# COSMETIC. No physics, no margin, no entrant, no score, no prediction sha is touched.
# Recorded, not repaired. No sealed file is edited (F44.1 route).

## WHAT WAS FOUND
`SESSION-63-COMBINED.md` (header) and `pack63/FAULT-F63.2-REPORTED-UNSHIPPED-RESULT.md`
both state the s63 tree as **1089/1089 root=MATCH**. `LINEAGE.txt` row 63 and the
open of this session both give **1091**:

    LINEAGE row 63    63    1091    9830f18a1522c1ceb4251edbc7ac5de7a0276b5dfdfe885bcf332edfd0fadda9
    open, s64         CONDENSE-CHECK s63: files=1091/1091 root=MATCH

## CAUSE — AND IT IS THE SAME CAUSE AS THE SECOND HALF OF F63.1
The arithmetic reconciles: 1089 + 2 = 1091. Two files entered `pack63/` after the
count was taken — `FAULT-F63.2-REPORTED-UNSHIPPED-RESULT.md` (which itself quotes
1089) and `SESSION-63-COMBINED.md`. **1089 is an intermediate count quoted in
documents that were then sealed into the tree they describe.**

This is exactly the shape of F63.1's second discrepancy, where
`pack61/RULING-F62.1-ADOPTED.md` quoted 1077 files and root 1ca50bff for a tree that
sealed at 1080 and dc77adda. **Third instance. 9830f18a… / 1091 is the operative s63
seal and is the one that verifies.**

## WHY IT IS ENTERED AT ALL, GIVEN THAT NOTHING IS WRONG WITH THE TREE
Because the previous instance of it cost a session its open. A quoted root that does
not verify is indistinguishable, on its face, from a tree that has been altered. A
reader who trusts the fault file's 1089 over LINEAGE's 1091 concludes the archive
gained two unaccounted files between the seal and the handoff. It did not; the two
files are the fault file and the combined handoff, and both are named in the tree.

It also has a live consequence for the class of fault F63.2 is about. F63.2's own
strongest argument is that a citation with no artefact behind it cannot be checked —
and F63.2 is itself the document quoting the stale count. The discipline is harder to
hold than the rule makes it sound: **a document that describes the tree it will be
sealed into cannot state that tree's size correctly from inside itself.**

## PROPOSED, FOR M
A structural remedy rather than a rule asking for more care:
  (a) A session states its tree count and root ONLY in `LINEAGE.txt`, which is written
      by the seal and not by hand, and every other document REFERS to the LINEAGE row
      rather than transcribing its numbers. s59's precedent — the root is not quoted
      in the bridge, it lives in the body of LINEAGE.txt — already does this for the
      root and should extend to the count.
  (b) Or the seal refuses to run when a file in `packN/` transcribes a root or count
      that disagrees with the row it is about to write. This is checkable: the seal
      knows both numbers at the moment it writes them.
(a) costs nothing and removes the failure mode rather than detecting it. Recommended.

## STATUS
OPEN, cosmetic, carried into the s64 seal. No repair attempted this session.
Any future citation of the s63 seal must use **9830f18a… / 1091**.

# F64.2 — A CHAIN ROW IS INDIVISIBLE AND SO IS NOT UNDER THE PRIME DIRECTIVE
# Raised 2026-08-20T20:04Z, SESSION 64, during the F63.2 re-run at Z=89.
# REPAIRED THIS SESSION. The repair is `pack64/tbstep.py` and it was can-failed
# against the sealed instrument before any row was scored on it.

## WHAT HAPPENED
Twice.

1. The four rows were first launched detached (`pack64/tb64.sh`, 19:52:17Z). The
   container terminated the background process between calls. Z=57 had COMPLETED —
   its full record was on disk in `.row57.tmp` — and was lost from the driver's
   accounting because the process died between the solve and the append.
2. Re-run in the foreground, Z=57 (108 s) and Z=58 (119 s) completed. **Z=89 did
   not.** It was killed at the wall-clock limit after ten of its fourteen channels
   had converged. Every one of those ten was discarded.

## THE DEFECT, NAMED PRECISELY
`nlchain.py restart Z` is ONE PROCESS PER ROW. It holds all fourteen channel solves
in a single unit of work that either completes or returns nothing. **A row is
therefore an atom that this project's own prime directive (§2.20) forbids: it does not
divide, it does not write intermediate results, and a rerun costs the whole row over
again including everything that had already succeeded.**

At Z <= 40 this never showed. Each row fitted a budget and the atom was never tested
against one. At Z = 89 the row is 310 s of compute across fourteen channels and it
does not fit, so the defect that was always there became visible. **This is a defect
of the harness, not of the physics, and it costs only time — but it costs it
repeatedly and silently, which is the shape §2.20 exists to prevent.**

## THE REPAIR
`pack64/tbstep.py`. It divides the row at its natural seam — the channel — and:
  * solves the reference once, caching E_ref, its iteration count and its guard rung

The reason is **f-channel orbital collapse**, and the evidence for it is already in the four sealed rows — but not in the form I put it in §4. My §4 wording is wrong and I'd withdraw it. Both things below.

**The reason.**

The tie-break clause presumes channel depth is a fixed function of (n, l): order by n+l, then by n, once, and carry it down the table. That presumption fails for f channels because their radial equation has a centrifugal barrier (l(l+1)/2r² = 12/r² for l=3) that admits two regimes — a diffuse outer-well state effectively outside the atom, and a compact inner-well state below the d channels. The f channel switches between them over one or two units of Z. There is no single (n, l) ordering to carry, because 4f is two different orbitals either side of the switch.

**The evidence, and it needs no new runs.** The rows carry their own ruler. Every g channel returns *exactly* the hydrogenic −1/2n²:

```
        5g -0.02000   6g -0.01389   7g -0.01021   8g -0.00781
        ratio to hydrogenic:  1.00   1.00   1.00   1.00
```

That is what a channel expelled beyond its barrier looks like: it sees the Z−1 electron cation as a point charge of +1 and binds like hydrogen. Against that ruler:

```
Z=57   4f  3.38x hydrogenic      5d  10.29x
Z=58   4f 11.74x                 5d  12.29x
Z=89   5f  1.57x                 6d  11.35x
Z=91   5f 15.27x                 6d  16.08x
```

**At Z=89 the 5f channel is 1.57× hydrogenic — it is barely inside the atom at all.** It doesn't lose the tie-break; it isn't in the room. Two units later it is 15×. The d channels sit at 10–16× throughout and never move regime. These are within-row comparisons at fixed Z and fixed reference, so nothing is confounded.

**What I got wrong.** §4 says the ordering "reverses as a function of what is already occupied." That is not established, and I should not have written it. Between Z=57 and Z=58 two things change together — nuclear charge 57→58 *and* the reference gains a 5d electron. I attributed the reversal to the second while the first moved underneath it. That is Standing 8 exactly: a comparison that did not hold its reference fixed. Sixth instance, and mine.

**What would separate them**, cheap and inside budget: hold the configuration fixed at the Ba-like …5p⁶6s² and solve 4f and 5d at nuclear charge 57, 58, 59. Occupancy constant, Z alone varying. If 4f collapses there, the driver is nuclear charge and my occupancy reading dies. Prediction filed before the run, per §2.13. Six solves.

**Bearing on ruling 2:** as it stands the assembly can say the tie-break is false at n+l = 7 and 8 and that the field is right. It cannot yet say *why* — the collapse account is standard physics and consistent with the ruler above, but this project has not measured ⟨r⟩ or the turning-point structure, and an energy ratio is not a radial extent. I'd keep the wording at "false where nature says so" until the fixed-Z control runs.

content.text:
The reason is **f-channel orbital collapse**, and the evidence for it is already in the four sealed rows — but not in the form I put it in §4. My §4 wording is wrong and I'd withdraw it. Both things below.

**The reason.**

The tie-break clause presumes channel depth is a fixed function of (n, l): order by n+l, then by n, once, and carry it down the table. That presumption fails for f channels because their radial equation has a centrifugal barrier (l(l+1)/2r² = 12/r² for l=3) that admits two regimes — a diffuse outer-well state effectively outside the atom, and a compact inner-well state below the d channels. The f channel switches between them over one or two units of Z. There is no single (n, l) ordering to carry, because 4f is two different orbitals either side of the switch.

**The evidence, and it needs no new runs.** The rows carry their own ruler. Every g channel returns *exactly* the hydrogenic −1/2n²:

```
        5g -0.02000   6g -0.01389   7g -0.01021   8g -0.00781
        ratio to hydrogenic:  1.00   1.00   1.00   1.00
```

That is what a channel expelled beyond its barrier looks like: it sees the Z−1 electron cation as a point charge of +1 and binds like hydrogen. Against that ruler:

```
Z=57   4f  3.38x hydrogenic      5d  10.29x
Z=58   4f 11.74x                 5d  12.29x
Z=89   5f  1.57x                 6d  11.35x
Z=91   5f 15.27x                 6d  16.08x
```

**At Z=89 the 5f channel is 1.57× hydrogenic — it is barely inside the atom at all.** It doesn't lose the tie-break; it isn't in the room. Two units later it is 15×. The d channels sit at 10–16× throughout and never move regime. These are within-row comparisons at fixed Z and fixed reference, so nothing is confounded.

**What I got wrong.** §4 says the ordering "reverses as a function of what is already occupied." That is not established, and I should not have written it. Between Z=57 and Z=58 two things change together — nuclear charge 57→58 *and* the reference gains a 5d electron. I attributed the reversal to the second while the first moved underneath it. That is Standing 8 exactly: a comparison that did not hold its reference fixed. Sixth instance, and mine.

**What would separate them**, cheap and inside budget: hold the configuration fixed at the Ba-like …5p⁶6s² and solve 4f and 5d at nuclear charge 57, 58, 59. Occupancy constant, Z alone varying. If 4f collapses there, the driver is nuclear charge and my occupancy reading dies. Prediction filed before the run, per §2.13. Six solves.

**Bearing on ruling 2:** as it stands the assembly can say the tie-break is false at n+l = 7 and 8 and that the field is right. It cannot yet say *why* — the collapse account is standard physics and consistent with the ruler above, but this project has not measured ⟨r⟩ or the turning-point structure, and an energy ratio is not a radial extent. I'd keep the wording at "false where nature says so" until the fixed-Z control runs.

Ruling on §4: withdraw and repair, or leave and annotate? It is unsealed, so either is available.

# ASSEMBLY REVISION — THE PASSAGES THE s64 CONTROL CHANGES
# SESSION 64. Item 3 of the s63 work list.
# `pack63/ASSEMBLY-RUNG-0.md` IS SEALED AND IS NOT EDITED (rule 4, F44.1 route).
# This file carries the exact replacement text for three passages and nothing else.
# It is written for M's ruling on the wording. Nothing here is adopted until ruled.

---

## R1 · ASSEMBLY §2, "THE CONSEQUENT RESTATEMENT" — REPLACE THE SECOND BULLET

WAS:
    * **THE TIE-BREAK CLAUSE IS AN EMPIRICAL REGULARITY OF THE LIGHT BLOCKS, NOT A
      LAW.** It is a property of the filling sequence, cannot be read off any single
      atom's spectrum, holds where n+l <= 6, and is false at n+l = 7 and 8 — where
      the field is right and the rule is wrong.

PROPOSED:
    * **THE TIE-BREAK CLAUSE IS AN EMPIRICAL REGULARITY OF THE LIGHT BLOCKS, NOT A
      LAW.** It is a property of the filling sequence, cannot be read off any single
      atom's spectrum, holds where n+l <= 6, and is false at n+l = 7 and 8 — where
      the field is right and the rule is wrong. **It is false under BOTH available
      references.** The chained rows build their own reference; the s64 controls
      (`pack64/tbctrl64.jsonl`, scored blind against a prediction sealed into the s63
      root) rebuild all four rows from the OBSERVED configuration of Z-1, and the
      departure survives: 5d over 4f at Z=57 by 100.29 mHa, 6d over 5f at Z=89 by
      126.16 mHa, entrant unchanged and ok=True at 4/4. **The departure is therefore
      not an artefact of the single-configuration reference.**

WHY THE ADDITION IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT DECORATION: as written in s63 the strongest
available objection to the project's central claim was that the walk's own build is
the thing departing from Madelung, not the field. That objection is now closed at the
four rows where the claim is made, and closed against a prediction it could not have
been fitted to.

---

## R2 · ASSEMBLY §3, THE LAST PARAGRAPH OF RUNG 2 — REPLACE

WAS:
    **RUNG 2 CLOSES AS A BOUND ON THE ORDERING AND ONLY ON THE ORDERING:** the
    single-determinant, average-of-configuration restriction displaces the entrant at
    11 of 107 rows, never at a row that opens a channel, and therefore changes nothing
    in the derived filling order. It is NOT closed as a bound on the row-by-row
    configuration, where its effect is measured above and is not small.

PROPOSED:
    **RUNG 2 CLOSES AS A BOUND ON THE ORDERING AND ONLY ON THE ORDERING:** the
    single-determinant, average-of-configuration restriction displaces the entrant at
    11 of 107 rows, never at a row that opens a channel, and therefore changes nothing
    in the derived filling order. It is NOT closed as a bound on the row-by-row
    configuration, where its effect is measured above and is not small.
    **THE BOUND IS TESTED DIRECTLY AT THE FOUR ROWS THAT CARRY THE MOST WEIGHT.** The
    pack53 instrument establishes the empty intersection but touches no first-entry
    row, so the immunity argument was structural rather than measured. s64 measures it
    where it matters: Z = 57, 58, 89, 91 are first-entry rows AND the rows the
    tie-break restatement rests on, and all four return the same entrant under the
    observed reference. **The immunity finding extends to blocks 7 and 8 rather than
    stopping at n+l <= 6.** Four rows are four rows; the other 16 first-entry rows are
    covered by the structural argument only, and that distinction is kept.

---

## R3 · ASSEMBLY §5, THE LEDGER — MOVE ONE LINE AND SHARPEN ANOTHER

Under **BOUNDED, WITH THE BOUND STATED**, REPLACE:
    * Single configuration (Rung 2): 11 of 107 rows displaced, none of them a
      first-entry row, ordering untouched.
WITH:
    * Single configuration (Rung 2): 11 of 107 rows displaced, none of them a
      first-entry row, ordering untouched. Measured directly at 4 first-entry rows
      (Z = 57, 58, 89, 91): entrant unchanged, 4/4, margins 32-126 mHa against a
      0.05 mHa floor. Structural elsewhere.

Under **OPEN, NAMED, NOT WORKED**, the line
    * L2: finite nuclear size and mass are not modelled and not bounded here.
STAYS, and is now **the only link in the twelve-link chain carrying no number.**
Recommend it be marked as such in the text, because a reader auditing the ledger
should be told where the single hole is rather than having to find it.

---

## R4 · WHAT IS NOT PROPOSED, AND WHY

**NO MECHANISM CLAIM IS ADDED.** The s64 rows show the f channel near-hydrogenic at
Z=89 (5f binds at 1.57x the hydrogenic value where every g channel returns exactly
1.00x) and fifteen times hydrogenic at Z=91. That is consistent with f-orbital
collapse and it is the natural reading. **It is not proposed for the assembly.** The
project has measured energies, not radial extents; an energy ratio is not an ⟨r⟩, and
this chain has a five-session record of the failure mode where a comparison is read
for more than it holds fixed. The assembly says the tie-break is false and that the
field is right. It does not say why, and should not until a fixed-reference control
separates nuclear charge from occupancy.

**THE s64 SCORE §4 IS WITHDRAWN AND REPAIRED** in the same movement: it read the four
rows in pairs and attributed the reversal to occupancy, where Z and occupancy moved
together. §2.12. The repaired text is the paragraph above.

L2 is one line in the chain: **the walk treats the nucleus as a point that never moves.** Real nuclei have size and weight. Neither is in the model.

**Why it matters:** the project's claim is that every shortcut from the exact Schrödinger equation has a price, and every price is far below the energy gaps the walk decides on. **To close it:** put a real nucleus in place of the point, re-run a few heavy rows, report the change in D against the 0.05 mHa floor. Two runs, prediction filed first.
